definitions.text: Uses cocaine, methamphetamine or misused stimulant pills in binges, more than planned.
Has strong cravings and crashes with exhaustion and low mood after use.
Use has caused health, money, work or legal problems, or periods of paranoia.

longTermGoals.text: The client reaches their own goal for stimulant use, stays safer from overdose and health harm, and rebuilds daily routines.

shortTermObjectives.text: Within 2 weeks, enroll in a program that offers contingency management, if available.
By the next session, have naloxone available, because the drug supply may contain fentanyl.
By session 3, set a personal use goal and list 3 reasons for change.
Use a coping skill for at least 3 cravings a week and record the outcome.
By session 8, complete a relapse prevention plan with high-risk situations, coping steps and support contacts.

problems.label: Building daily life, relationships and supports that make change in stimulant use last

definitions.text: Most free time, friends or routines are linked to stimulant use, and other rewarding activities have dropped away.
Has few people who support the change, or relationships at home are strained by use.

longTermGoals.text: The client has rewarding activities, relationships and supports that fit the goal they chose.

shortTermObjectives.text: With a clinician trained in the community reinforcement approach, by week 6 plan at least 2 rewarding activities a week without stimulant (for example work, social or leisure) and a trial period without use that the client agrees to.

By week 4, explore mutual-help options that fit the client (for example NA, SMART Recovery, or faith-based or culturally specific groups) and, if interested, attend at least 1 meeting and talk it over at the next session.
If the client has a partner who supports the change and there is no abuse or coercive control, discuss by week 4 behavioral couples therapy, and refer if it fits.
Over weeks 3 to 10, go through 1 recent episode of use every 2 weeks step by step (what came before, thoughts, feelings, urges and what followed) and agree on 1 change.

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit. Every item in this plan records substance use: the export carries the 42 CFR Part 2 notice.
